question: Can current non-mutating GitHub provider metadata provide a stateless, unforgeable monotonic repository-incarnation lower bound that survives delete/recreate, rename/transfer and rollback without retaining predecessor state or using paid/external coordination?
tested_scope: One bounded official-GitHub provider-side identity/history leaf: current REST repository metadata plus official rename, transfer, and deleted-repository restoration semantics. No mutation, no other-role state, no downstream/O state, no hosted compute, no paid feature consumption.

official_sources.negative_observation: The current response exposes current repository identity/metadata but no predecessor_repository_id, incarnation counter, deleted-predecessor list, or monotonic retirement floor.

official_sources.observation: GitHub documents restoration of eligible deleted repositories within 90 days; fork-network support restoration can require a paid GitHub plan. This is bounded/privileged recovery, not a permanent stateless incarnation witness.
GitHub redirects old repository locations after rename, but explicitly warns that creating a new repository under the original name makes redirects to the renamed repository stop working.
GitHub redirects the previous repository location after transfer, but creating a new repository or fork at the previous location permanently deletes those redirects.

counterexample.world_A: Logical path X currently resolves to repository R2 with current metadata M2 and no relevant predecessor exists.
counterexample.world_B: Logical path X previously resolved to R1; R1 was renamed/transferred/deleted, then a new repository R2 was created at X after the old redirect/history became unavailable.
counterexample.current_observation: A stateless non-mutating GET of X can return the same current R2 metadata M2 in both worlds.
counterexample.consequence: Any authority decision that is only a function of current repository metadata cannot distinguish whether a predecessor incarnation existed, so it cannot prove a monotonic incarnation/retirement lower bound across the required resurrection scope.

required_negative_matrix.lost_predecessor_id: FAIL: current metadata contains only current identifiers; without retained predecessor ID/history, prior incarnation existence is not recoverable from this response.
required_negative_matrix.name_reuse: FAIL: official rename docs state original-name reuse breaks the old redirect, allowing the logical name to denote a new repository without carrying forward the prior alias witness.
required_negative_matrix.transfer_or_rename: FAIL as permanent proof: redirects preserve reachability only while the previous location is not reused; current full_name is identity metadata, not a monotonic incarnation floor.
required_negative_matrix.restore_window_expiry: FAIL: documented deleted-repository restoration is bounded to 90 days for eligible repositories; it does not establish indefinite predecessor discoverability.
required_negative_matrix.private_or_deleted_predecessor_invisibil: FAIL in tested current-endpoint scope: current GET exposes no deleted/predecessor list; no positive proof was found that a deleted/private predecessor remains discoverable from current public repository metadata.
required_negative_matrix.paid_or_admin_only_route: REJECT: restoration is owner/admin recovery and some fork-network support restoration requires a paid plan; such a route cannot be the zero-dependency authority mechanism.
required_negative_matrix.rate_limit_interruption: FAIL-CLOSED: if the current metadata GET is unavailable/rate-limited, no incarnation authority is granted; repository transport is not treated as compute or as a reason to weaken the fence.
required_negative_matrix.mutative_probe: PASS constraint: this leaf used no mutation and requires no mutation for its negative result.
required_negative_matrix.zero_finite_monthly_trial_paid_quota: No accepted candidate: the tested current metadata path itself adds no monthly/trial/paid dependency, but it is insufficient to prove incarnation history.
required_negative_matrix.zero_incremental_cost: PASS for the bounded test: no incremental monetary cost was introduced.

scope_guard: This falsifies only the documented/current GitHub REST repository-metadata plus rename/transfer/restore route as a stateless incarnation-floor proof. It does not claim undocumented/internal/future provider metadata cannot exist.
minimal_unresolved_child: A provider-side monotonic predecessor/incarnation witness that remains discoverable after logical-name reuse and predecessor deletion/restore expiry, is non-mutating and queryable from current state without retaining predecessor identity, and requires no paid/finite quota or external storage.
continuation: Part93: execute exactly one bounded official-GitHub owner/provider-history leaf testing whether the public user/repository event surfaces and repository-ID lookup/redirect semantics can recover a prior repository incarnation after logical-name reuse without a retained predecessor ID. Required negatives: event retention truncation, no-event periods, private/deleted predecessor, rename/transfer then name reuse, known-old-ID versus lost-old-ID, API rate-limit interruption, no mutation, zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota and zero incremental cost. Accept only a non-mutating provider witness that is sufficient under lost-predecessor-ID; otherwise persist the exact history-gap boundary and select a distinct next provider-side authority leaf for the following invocation.
